$comment: check:hermetic-tests' exception table for integra-protocol, held in the TREE rather than inside the gate: a table baked into a script makes the gate undrivable, because it can only ever run against the one tree whose hosts it already lists. Each namedNotCalled key is a non-loopback host a NON-LIVE test names — or that a module such a test imports names — with the reason it is a value rather than a call. Adding an entry is a claim that the host is never fetched; read the occurrence before making it. CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: an unlisted host fails, and a listed host that appears nowhere fails. NOTE: a live rail harness here is integration*.test.ts, not commerce's *.live.test.ts — see live-harness-files.mjs.

namedNotCalled.93.184.216.34: A STUBBED DNS LOOKUP RESULT, not a destination. `resolver.test.ts` injects both the lookup and `fetchImpl`, and this address is the stand-in for 'some public address' against which the hardened resolver's refusals are proven — beside 169.254.169.254, the cloud metadata address the resolver must refuse. Nothing is dialled; the point of the suite is which addresses are REJECTED.
namedNotCalled.api.blockcypher.com: ⭐ THE PLANTED DEFECT INSIDE THIS GATE'S OWN DRIVE, and nothing else in the tree. `rail-invariants/test/hermetic-tests-invariant.test.ts` writes this host into TEMPORARY fixture trees and asserts the gate refuses it — in a test file, and in a helper a test imports. It is never fetched: the drive's fixtures are `mkdtemp` directories the gate reads and nothing executes. ⚠️ It needs an entry here only because this repository's drives live under `packages/`, which the gate walks; the sibling repository's drives sit in `scripts/`, outside its own subject set. ⛔ Closed in both directions: if the drive stops planting this host, this entry goes stale and the gate refuses it — so the exemption cannot outlive the plant.

$comment2: Every THIRD-PARTY import a non-live test makes, classified. A host scan cannot see a client that takes its address from process.env, so every import is accounted for as one of three kinds. inert: it reaches no network at all. addressed-in-source: it can, and any endpoint it is pointed at is written in the file, where the host scan sees it — loopback included, which this gate declares hermetic. endpoint-from-environment: it can, and its address does NOT appear in the file, so a test importing one MUST gate itself on the variable it needs or be a live rail harness. CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Classifications for packages this repository shares with integra-agentic-commerce are carried across with their reasons rather than re-derived; the four multiformats/bs58 entries are this repository's own.

@aptos-labs/ts-sdk.why: a chain client whose node URL is written into the fixture that builds it

@cfworker/json-schema.why: a JSON-Schema validator; it dereferences nothing

@mysten/sui/transactions.why: transaction construction; the client that would submit one is a separate subpath this suite does not import

bs58.why: Base58 encode/decode and nothing else. binding-solana's `src/adapter.ts` imports the same module to read a key pair out of its textual form; there is no transport in it.

multiformats/cid.why: CID construction. `evidence/src/car.ts` imports the same module to build content identifiers for a CAR file; multiformats is deliberately transport-free — fetching a CID is a different package.

multiformats/codecs/raw.why: The raw multicodec, a two-function encoder. Same import as `evidence/src/car.ts`.

multiformats/hashes/digest.why: Multihash digest construction from bytes already in hand. Same import as `evidence/src/car.ts`.

node:child_process.why: ⚠️ it can spawn anything, including something that reaches a network. What bounds it is the command, which is written in the file — this gate reads the imports, and a reviewer reads the command

node:http.why: used to BIND a loopback server, which this gate declares hermetic in its own head note — and any address it is pointed at is a string the host scan reads

node:module.why: `createRequire` for resolving a path. No transport.

node:process.why: argv, env and exit. No transport.

node:url.why: URL parsing — parsing an address is not dialling one

node:zlib.why: gunzip of a tarball already in hand. No transport.

viem.why: the EVM client. A transport is constructed from a URL the file states, or from an injected port

viem/accounts.why: key derivation and signing, no transport
